title: Vajda's and d'Ocagne's Identities for Fibonacci Numbers
description: Vajda's identity is the two-parameter master identity of the Fibonacci product family: over the integer Fibonacci sequence Int.fib, Fₓ₊ᵢ·Fₓ₊ⱼ − Fₓ·Fₓ₊ᵢ₊ⱼ = (−1)^|x|·Fᵢ·Fⱼ for all integers x, i, j. Mathlib (Monica Omar, 2025) records Cassini's identity and Catalan's identity over Int.fib, but not their common two-parameter generalization Vajda, nor d'Ocagne's identity Fₘ·Fₙ₊₁ − Fₘ₊₁·Fₙ = (−1)^|n|·Fₘ₋ₙ. This entry supplies both. The proof of Vajda mirrors Mathlib's own Catalan proof: the three shifted Fibonacci numbers Fₓ₊ᵢ, Fₓ₊ⱼ, Fₓ₊ᵢ₊ⱼ are expanded with the integer addition formula Int.fib_add, the inner Fᵢ₊ⱼ and Fᵢ₊ⱼ₊₁ are expanded the same way, and the whole expression collapses — by ring-level algebra together with Cassini's identity for x — to (−1)^|x|·Fᵢ·Fⱼ. d'Ocagne (x = n, i = m−n, j = 1) and fresh derivations of Catalan (i = j) and Cassini (i = j = 1) are then immediate corollaries, recovering the full classical hierarchy from a single theorem.

meta.author: Steven Vajda / Maurice d'Ocagne (19th–20th c.); formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib

mathlibDependencies.description: fib (m + n) = fib (m − 1) · fib n + fib m · fib (n + 1) — the integer Fibonacci addition formula; applied five times to expand every shifted term in Vajda's identity
Cassini's identity fib (n + 1) · fib (n − 1) − fib n ^ 2 = (−1)^|n| — used to substitute the alternating sign (−1)^|x| and reduce Vajda to a pure ring identity
fib (n + 2) = fib n + fib (n + 1) — the defining integer Fibonacci recurrence, used to normalize the shifted indices fib (x+1), fib (i+1), fib (j+1+1)
fib 1 = 1 — collapses the Fⱼ = F₁ factor when specializing Vajda to d'Ocagne and Cassini

originalContributions: fib_vajda: ∀ x i j : ℤ, fib (x+i)·fib (x+j) − fib x·fib (x+i+j) = (−1)^|x|·(fib i·fib j) — Vajda's two-parameter identity, absent from Mathlib
fib_dOcagne: ∀ m n : ℤ, fib m·fib (n+1) − fib (m+1)·fib n = (−1)^|n|·fib (m−n) — d'Ocagne's identity, absent from Mathlib, obtained as the (x=n, i=m−n, j=1) case of Vajda

fib_catalan: ∀ x a : ℤ, fib (x+a)² − fib x·fib (x+2a) = (−1)^|x|·fib a² — Catalan's identity recovered as the i=j case of Vajda (matching Mathlib's independent Int.fib_add_sq_sub_fib_mul_fib_add_two_mul)
fib_cassini: ∀ x : ℤ, fib (x+1)² − fib x·fib (x+2) = (−1)^|x| — Cassini's identity recovered as the i=j=1 case of Vajda
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (only Mathlib's foundational propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound). No decide/native_decide is used.

overview.historicalContext: The Fibonacci product identities form a hierarchy. At the bottom sits Cassini's identity (1680), Fₙ₋₁Fₙ₊₁ − Fₙ² = (−1)ⁿ. Catalan's identity Fₙ² − Fₙ₋ᵣFₙ₊ᵣ = (−1)ⁿ⁻ʳFᵣ² adds one parameter, and at the top sits Vajda's identity Fₙ₊ᵢFₙ₊ⱼ − FₙFₙ₊ᵢ₊ⱼ = (−1)ⁿFᵢFⱼ (named for Steven Vajda, whose 1989 monograph systematized these relations), which contains Catalan as the diagonal case i = j, Cassini as i = j = 1, and d'Ocagne's identity FₘFₙ₊₁ − Fₘ₊₁Fₙ = (−1)ⁿFₘ₋ₙ (Maurice d'Ocagne) as the case j = 1. Mathlib's Int.fib library records Cassini and Catalan but stops short of the master identity; this entry supplies Vajda and d'Ocagne and re-derives the rest, all over the two-sided integer Fibonacci sequence so the identities hold at negative indices as well.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (fibonacci-identities-oq-04)**: Prove the two-parameter master identity of the Fibonacci product family — Vajda's identity — and derive d'Ocagne's, Catalan's, and Cassini's identities from it.

**Result**: fib_vajda (fib (x+i)·fib (x+j) − fib x·fib (x+i+j) = (−1)^|x|·(fib i·fib j)) together with fib_dOcagne, fib_catalan, and fib_cassini as one-line corollaries.
overview.text: For all integers x, i, j, working over the integer Fibonacci sequence Int.fib, Fₓ₊ᵢ·Fₓ₊ⱼ − Fₓ·Fₓ₊ᵢ₊ⱼ = (−1)^|x|·Fᵢ·Fⱼ. The two free offsets i, j make this the most general of the elementary Fibonacci product identities: every classical special case is recovered by fixing them.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Proof Strategy.**

1. Expand the three shifted Fibonacci numbers with the integer addition formula Int.fib_add: Fₓ₊ᵢ = Fₓ₋₁Fᵢ + FₓFᵢ₊₁, similarly for Fₓ₊ⱼ, and Fₓ₊₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎ = Fₓ₋₁Fᵢ₊ⱼ + FₓFᵢ₊ⱼ₊₁ after normalizing x+i+j to x+(i+j).
2. Expand the inner products Fᵢ₊ⱼ = Fᵢ₋₁Fⱼ + FᵢFⱼ₊₁ and Fᵢ₊₍ⱼ₊₁₎ = Fᵢ₋₁Fⱼ₊₁ + FᵢFⱼ₊₂ with Int.fib_add again (normalizing i+j+1 to i+(j+1)).
3. Replace the alternating sign (−1)^|x| by its Cassini value Fₓ₊₁Fₓ₋₁ − Fₓ² (rw ← Int.fib_succ_mul_fib_pred_sub_fib_sq), eliminating the only non-polynomial atom.
4. Apply the recurrence in the forms Fₓ₊₁ = Fₓ₋₁ + Fₓ, Fᵢ₊₁ = Fᵢ₋₁ + Fᵢ, Fⱼ₊₁₊₁ = Fⱼ + Fⱼ₊₁ to put every index into a canonical base set {Fₓ₋₁, Fₓ, Fᵢ, Fᵢ₋₁, Fⱼ, Fⱼ₊₁}. What remains is a polynomial identity closed by `ring`: the cross terms collapse to (Fₓ₋₁² + Fₓ₋₁Fₓ − Fₓ²)·FᵢFⱼ, and the Cassini coefficient is exactly (−1)^|x|.
5. Corollaries: d'Ocagne is fib_vajda n (m−n) 1 (then n+(m−n) = m, n+(m−n)+1 = m+1, F₁ = 1); Catalan is fib_vajda x a a (then x+a+a = x+2a); Cassini is fib_vajda x 1 1. Each closes by linear_combination against the specialized Vajda instance.
keyInsights: **One identity, four classical theorems.** Vajda's two free offsets i, j specialize to Catalan (i = j), Cassini (i = j = 1), and d'Ocagne (j = 1, x = n, i = m−n), so a single proof yields the whole elementary hierarchy.

**Cassini is the only arithmetic input.** After the Int.fib_add expansions every Fibonacci-specific fact is gone except the alternating sign; substituting Cassini's identity for (−1)^|x| turns the goal into a pure ring identity — the same reduction Mathlib uses for Catalan, now carried through with two parameters.

**Index normalization is the subtlety.** Int.fib_add emits indices like i+(j+1) and j+1+1; matching the recurrence rewrites to exactly those syntactic forms (rather than the visually simpler j+2) is what makes the final `ring` fire.

**Genuinely beyond Mathlib.** Mathlib's Int.fib file has Cassini and Catalan but neither Vajda nor d'Ocagne; both are supplied here over the two-sided integer Fibonacci sequence, valid at negative indices.

**Corollaries are one-liners, not fresh proofs.** Once fib_vajda is established, fib_dOcagne, fib_catalan, and fib_cassini each follow from a single `linear_combination h` after renaming the compound index by `ring` (plus, where a factor fib 1 appears, one `simp` to collapse it to 1) — no case analysis on the sign and no repeated appeal to Int.fib_add, so the entire classical hierarchy below Vajda is pure linear algebra over one instantiated hypothesis.
prerequisites: The integer Fibonacci addition formula Int.fib_add and recurrence Int.fib_add_two
The ring and linear_combination tactics for closing polynomial identities

sections.mathContext: $F_{x+i}F_{x+j} - F_x F_{x+i+j} = (-1)^{|x|} F_i F_j$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, with $F$ the two-sided integer Fibonacci sequence.

sections.title: Vajda's Identity
sections.summary: fib_vajda: the master theorem. Five Int.fib_add expansions reduce the two-parameter product to base atoms; substituting Cassini's identity for (−1)^|x| and applying the recurrence leaves a `ring` identity.

sections.title: d'Ocagne's Identity
sections.summary: fib_dOcagne: the (x=n, i=m−n, j=1) specialization, with n+(m−n) collapsing to m and F₁ = 1, closed by linear_combination against the Vajda instance.

sections.title: Catalan's Identity (recovered)
sections.summary: fib_catalan: the diagonal i = j = a case, recovering the statement of Mathlib's independent Int.fib_add_sq_sub_fib_mul_fib_add_two_mul from the master identity.

sections.title: Cassini's Identity (recovered)
sections.summary: fib_cassini: the i = j = 1 case, recovering Cassini's identity over Int.fib from the master identity.

crossReferences.description: The oq-01 Cassini entry (over Nat.fib) lists Catalan's and d'Ocagne's identities as open questions; this entry resolves both as corollaries of the more general Vajda identity over Int.fib

conclusion.summary: Complete, fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms) proof of Vajda's two-parameter Fibonacci identity over the integer Fibonacci sequence, together with d'Ocagne's identity and re-derivations of Catalan's and Cassini's identities as one-line corollaries.
conclusion.implications: Adds the master identity of the elementary Fibonacci product family — and d'Ocagne's identity — to the formalized record, both absent from Mathlib's Int.fib library, and demonstrates that Cassini and Catalan are uniform specializations of a single two-parameter theorem.
openQuestions: Prove Vajda's identity for the Lucas numbers and the general Gibonacci (Horadam) sequences, where the sign constant is replaced by a discriminant.
Formalize the matrix form det([[1,1],[1,0]]ⁿ) = (−1)ⁿ and deduce Vajda from the Cauchy–Binet / multiplicativity of determinants.
Prove the Gelin–Cesàro identity Fₙ₋₂Fₙ₋₁Fₙ₊₁Fₙ₊₂ − Fₙ⁴ = −1, a fourth-degree relative obtainable by combining two Catalan instances.
